Subject: RFQ clarification: DPA timelines and approvals

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — features and perf looked great. Procurement is moving this along but we have two asks before we can open a PO: a) a simple approval matrix showing which internal stakeholders at Redwood are responsible for DPA execution, subprocessor onboarding, and KMS attestations; and b) an expected timeline from signed DPA to subprocessor evidence delivery (we often need artefacts for our security review).

To help with our procurement window, can you provide a short, authoritative matrix we can attach to the Purchase Order and an estimate for when we’ll be able to hand over KMS and subprocessor attestations after signing? We’re aiming to finalize budgets by 6/21.

Appreciate it — if easier, a quick call today would work.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Lorenzo
Sr. Procurement Manager
MedixOne

Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFQ clarification: DPA timelines and approvals

Hi Ava — thanks for the note and the clear asks. I’m looping in Connor (Legal ops) and Marissa (Privacy lead) to make sure we provide exactly what you need.

High level answers up front:
- Approval matrix: we’ll provide a one-page matrix that maps Redwood roles to DPA responsibilities (who signs, who approves subprocessor additions, who owns KMS attestations).
- Timeline: typical turnaround from mutual DPA signature to delivery of subprocessor evidence and KMS attestation is 7-14 business days for standard enterprise engagements. If you need expedited evidence (under 5 business days) we can prioritize with our Evidence Team but will need a signed PO or a procurement holdback to cover analyst time.

Next steps: Connor will attach the matrix and our proposed redlines to the DPA. Marissa will add estimated delivery milestones against each artifact. Expect the first PDF and an editable approval_matrix_v1.xlsx by EOD 6/8.

If you’d like a 30-minute call to walk through the matrix and timeline, propose times and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment references: will attach approval_matrix_v1.xlsx and redline_dpa_medixone_20260608.pdf in follow-up

Thanks Evelyn — that timeline works in principle. A couple of clarifying Qs from legal (cc’d previously):
1) For KMS attestations, do you provide a customer-specific key custody statement or a general attestation that your key management practices meet industry standards? We need something we can attach to an internal security memo.
2) For subprocessors: will the approval matrix show which class of subprocessor (e.g., analytics, cloud infra, telemetry) each team manages, or will you enumerate named subprocessors in the artifact?
3) If your redlines are substantive, will you accept our legal team’s redline to the DPA or do you require a call with Legal first?

If it helps, we can share the specific language we prefer for KMS custody and a template PO note for procurement that references the approval matrix.

Best,
Ava

Hi Ava — Connor here from Legal Ops. Attaching the two artifacts we discussed: a) a one-page approval_matrix_v1.xlsx that maps internal roles (Legal, Privacy, Security, Product) to DPA actions and authority; and b) a redline PDF of our standard DPA with notes on three common clauses (subprocessor onboarding, cross-border transfer exhibits, and KMS attestation language).

Short answers to your Qs:
1) KMS attestation: we provide a customer-specific attestation letter that confirms key custody model (Redwood-managed keys vs. customer-managed keys via KMS integration) and enumerates the controls we maintain. That letter is drafted once the DPA and deployment model are agreed and is delivered within the 7-14 business day window.
2) Subprocessors: the approval matrix will show categories and primary owners; we also provide a named subprocessor exhibit (CSV list) as an attachment to the DPA for procurement purposes. The exhibit is updated during onboarding and delivered alongside the evidence pack.
3) Redlines: we are happy to take your legal team's redline. If the redlines are materially different from our standard terms we typically ask for a 30-minute legal sync to accelerate resolution, but we will accept a redline for review first.

We’ve marked expedited lanes in the embedded matrix if you need faster delivery (costs/time to be confirmed). Please review the attachments and let me know whether MedixOne would like a legal sync or to proceed via redline exchange.

Connor O’Brien
Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
